qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Consolidated 5-year median GAAP ROIC is depressed to 7-10% (failing the mandatory 12% hurdle) due to the $16.6B Mead Johnson acquisition goodwill, subsequent multi-billion pound write-downs, and severe infant formula litigation liabilities. Outside of core OTC health, price increases in home hygiene triggered volume declines and market share losses to private label.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3b = N, REJECT). Global consumer health and hygiene portfolio carries brand intangibles, but consolidated 5-year GAAP ROIC of 7-10% fails the 12% threshold, permanently scarred by the disastrous $16.6B Mead Johnson acquisition and subsequent write-downs. Price hikes in non-health categories resulted in negative volumes, demonstrating limited pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Acquisition of Mead Johnson in 2017 for $16.6B bloated balance sheet with goodwill and intangibles, triggering successive multi-billion pound impairments and depressing consolidated ROIC below 10% for nearly a decade. Core OTC brands (Nurofen, Strepsils, Gaviscon) have strong margins, but volume elasticity across Essential Home and infant nutrition litigation overhang led to multi-year underperformance and CEO turnover.
